title: Article 148 — Comptroller and Auditor-General of India

content.overview: Article 148 provides that there shall be a Comptroller and Auditor-General of India appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal, who shall only be removed from office in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. The CAG’s salary and other conditions of service are determined by Parliament by law and cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment. The CAG is not eligible for further office under the Government of India or of any State after he has ceased to hold office. Expenses of the CAG’s office are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
content.glance: CAG appointed by President; removal like SC Judge; conditions not varied to disadvantage after appointment; no further government office after demitting office; expenses charged on Consolidated Fund of India.
content.study:
Article 148 establishes the CAG as an independent constitutional authority:
1. Appointment by the President.
2. Removal only in like manner and on like grounds as a Supreme Court Judge.
3. Salary and conditions by parliamentary law; not varied to disadvantage after appointment.
4. Ineligible for further office under Union or State Government after ceasing to hold office.
5. Administrative expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

Examination: independence safeguards; parallel to SC Judge removal; charged expenditure; post-office bar.

sections.heading: Independence safeguards
sections.body:
1. Appointed by President.
2. Removal only like a Supreme Court Judge.
3. Conditions not varied to disadvantage after appointment.
4. No further Union/State government office after demitting office.
5. Expenses charged on Consolidated Fund of India.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How is the Comptroller and Auditor-General appointed and protected under Article 148?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 148, the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal and can be removed from office only in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. The CAG’s salary and conditions of service are determined by Parliament by law and shall not be varied to his disadvantage after appointment. After ceasing to hold office, the CAG is not eligible for further office under the Government of India or of any State. The administrative expenses of the CAG’s office are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
